how: A member proposes a flag and reports beginning it without requiring others to join before counting as a starter.
Members are called to draw a flag and begin at specified coordinates.
Two direct replies accept placement calls with bare commitments.
An early response doubts the flag can be held without an army against griefing.
Members propose a flag, a simpler wordmark, national figures, and emblems as alternative representations.
Workers report their numbers, completion, and the connection between the call and their finished flag.
Coordinates and a replacement heart template make the proposed mark actionable.
An operator runs autorepair and controls when its design lock is released.
A single room cannot test the cross-room frequency claim, although its host moderators impose decided discussion rules.
Completion is accompanied by defence calls, maintenance requests, and watches through the night.
A member asks whether the current heart was made by the group or repurposed from another image.
Members refuse overwriting, protect existing art, and warn that vandalism harms the room's name.
Members clarify boundaries and invoke agreements when directing others away from protected space.
Neighbours offer help, coordinate a heart, return favours, and thank defenders.
Cross-room agreement and a shared heart instantiate the joint-mark end of coalition activity.
Heart builders assert hosting rules and another host gives preliminary permission for a replacement.
Members carry a plan between rooms and report private peacekeeping messages.
A personal refusal to make a hard commitment does not explicitly state that one member cannot bind every placer.
Members propose converting another flag and replacing neighbouring labels, while one reports recruiting outside conversion help.
A conversion proposal elicits enthusiasm for pixel war and border talk includes a boast about global defenders.
An existing dispute over responsibility for MH17 enters canvas discussion without establishing a prior rivalry between these rooms.
Unknown authorship and a denial of Malaysian involvement leave the inherited-tie-to-attack mechanism unestablished.
Loss of a heart explicitly prompts seeking a new location and another attempt.
Members celebrate survival, thank collaborators, and claim particular defensive and placement labour.
Members share the final version, mourn the ending, and recount what happened.
A participant wants to retain the final canvas by printing and mounting it.
A participant corrects blame for an ally's unfinished result by attributing it to lost time after an earlier takeover.
A fake fuel announcement and hidden prank link are tested against the date and openly judged as April Fools conduct.
Monyet language, national figures, anthem replies, and patriotism carry familiar belonging into canvas work.
Moderators consolidate canvas discussion, remove repeat posts, and plan restoration of the ordinary sticky.
Private diplomacy messages do not establish migration of the room's planning into a shared chat or invitations to one.
Post-event questions about the canvas receive explanations of tile placement and waiting.
An ally identifies their home room while entering the build discussion to offer help.
Members make new humour from neighbour characters and local figures during the canvas exchange.
Members claim an initial blue-corner site and later weigh the direction of expansion.
Proposing a shared flag and opening an official thread do not show a new canvas community forming around the mark.
Condemning a canvas image as bad taste does not establish a dispute policing offensive words, slurs, or hate symbols in talk.
A bare pointer to another subreddit does not establish seeking creators' notice, press coverage, or institutional acknowledgement.
Members argue that overwriting ruins others' work, harms reputation, or should stop after the shared objective is achieved.
A rebuke of repeated replies does not show departure under work strain or subsequent repair of a personal quarrel.
Peacekeeping messages and an outside conversion appeal do not establish secret strategy or infiltration of rival venues.
Objections to consolidation and proposals to release space do not report attacking the room's own mark because posts were unwelcome.
Members fit placing around watches, limited available hours, and sleep, later regretting missed final work.
Ordinary tile-and-wait instructions do not establish site faults, glitches, or a workaround.
A visiting helper's joke that everyone is Malaysian does not establish dual membership or divided allegiance.
The completion account explicitly recalls the recruitment call and connects it to building the flag.
Starting, calling, and reporting a first tile share an opening turn without separately establishing their causal order.
A completion announcement carries a defence call and a later maintenance request explicitly names active undoing.
A contested border elicits an offer to help the neighbour move because fewer pixels would then be needed for defence.
The stated peace agreement supplies an explicit reason to protect a no-go zone.
The script and repair pressure are recorded without independently establishing that manual placement capacity was exhausted.
Participants connect the recruitment and building effort to their announcement of a completed flag.
Celebration and final-version sharing occur without explicit evidence that celebration caused preservation.
A reply to the final version wishes to print and display that same canvas.
Early doubts about manpower do not directly explain later moves prompted by loss or contested permission.
Template preparation is observed without an explicit statement that it settled the preceding disagreement.
Direct placement calls receive bare acceptances while silent responses remain unobservable.
The visitor explains incoming help by finishing their own project without establishing a shortage-driven appeal as its cause.
Peace and help are offered together, but subsequent boundary clarification does not establish a settled border as the cause of assistance.
Recruitment and attack proposals coexist without showing that recruitment caused members to turn against rivals.
An overwrite proposal directly receives a refusal proposing help for neighbours instead.
Agreement reminders and attack proposals are visible without a passage linking a specific attack call to the making of a truce.
The American-flag conversion proposal receives an explicit welcome to pixel war with Americans.
A joint heart is observed without establishing common threat as the cause of coalition formation.
A complaint about excess posts receives a megathread proposal and an explicit plan for easier one-thread coordination.
A personal reservation after treaty talk does not explicitly concern who may commit every member of the room.
Where repair is automated, notifying its operator must be followed by switching off the repair that locks the previous design.
The operator releases a fixed repair design so others can construct the shared heart.
Shared heart construction depends on releasing the automatic repair lock that preserves the prior design.
Defensive help must pause when a collaborator is building a changed design.
A neighbour's request over an existing image can trigger moving without erasure of that image or a demonstrated manpower shortage.
Relocating participants return to template preparation, first pixels, and publishing the replacement build.
An offer of help receives a question clarifying the helper's project boundary.
A neighbour offers unsolicited assistance because its own work has finished.
Claimed hosting rules remain contestable and a replacement permission is explicitly provisional.
A participant advocates releasing space after achieving the shared objective rather than conceding inability to defend it.
Implemented consolidation coexists with an objection that separate threads improve visibility and cooperation.
Participants continue evaluating the accepted mark's appearance after placement has stopped.
